title: Ordinary localized projection inverse mate is invertible
statement: Let X,Y be schemes, f:X → Y a morphism, R_Y,R_X pro-étale coefficient ring sheaves in the containing universe, c:f*R_Y ≅ R_X, and g a Global operation package [def-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-restriction-data]. Fix V in Y.ProEt and a LocalBaseData package b [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-local-base-data]. For any ordinary direct-image comparison g.pushforward followed by restriction to V ≅ restriction to f*V followed by b.pushforward whose maps are identity on every section, its inverse mate under the specified ordinary module adjunctions is invertible.

source.place: Tag 04J0, lemma-localize-morphism-ringed-sites; canonical inverse-image comparison and its unit normalization.

proof.text: The coefficient_sections field identifies the local coefficient morphism with locMap of the global morphism. The pro-étale base-change functor preserves finite limits. Apply the containing-universe localization theorem: product comparison identifies the composite right adjoints and uniqueness of their left adjoints makes localComparison invertible.

For each module, apply the local adjunction hom-equivalence to the inverse mate and to localComparison. The unit mate equation identifies the first adjunct with the restricted global unit followed by the specified direct-image comparison. Its section identity removes that last comparison. The adjunct of localComparison is exactly the restricted global unit. Injectivity identifies the components; hence all components of the inverse mate are invertible. This uses no derived-category or shift assertion and includes zero modules and zero coefficient rings.

proof_origin.place: Tag 04J0; specialization of the existing containing-universe localization comparison and the adjunction unit mate formula.
